practices/0002: No automated check enforces README/AGENTS.md content boundaries; this is a documentation convention followed by review, not a mechanically-checkable rule.
practices/0003: No automated check can distinguish an @import an author correctly treats as eager from one they mistakenly assume is lazy; enforcement is left to review, since the gap is in an author's belief, not the file's structure.
practices/0004: No automated check can detect a contradiction in meaning between two instructions; enforcement is left to review, since spotting a substantive conflict requires understanding what each rule says, not just its shape.
practices/0005: No automated check can tell whether a SKILL.md's body and reference files actually follow relevance-gated loading and one level of reference depth; enforcement is left to review, since that requires reading what the files say, not just that they exist.
practices/0006: No automated check can determine whether an instruction actually needed the on-demand nested or path-scoped loading model rather than the root file; enforcement is left to review, since the judgment depends on how narrow the guidance is, not on file structure alone.
practices/0007: No automated check can tell which layer's ranking an author assumed when writing a personal- or project-level instruction; enforcement is left to review, since the gap is in an author's belief about precedence, not the file's structure.
practices/0008: No automated check can tell whether a line of prose was chosen instead of a hook or a permissions.deny rule out of genuine judgment or oversight; enforcement is left to review, since distinguishing the two requires understanding what the instruction needs to guarantee.
practices/0009: No automated check can judge whether a SKILL.md's description actually states what the skill does and when to use it, or whether it reads in the third person; enforcement is left to review, since that requires reading the description's content, not just its presence.
practices/0010: No automated check enforces a CLAUDE.md line-count target for a project outside this repository; enforcement is left to review, since the check this repository itself runs (instruction-limits) only bounds this repository's own files.
practices/0011: No automated check can inspect a hook script written for a project outside this repository to confirm it exits 2 rather than 1 on a policy violation; enforcement is left to review, since that requires reading what the hook script actually does.
practices/0012: No automated check can measure whether a project's loaded context is small enough; enforcement is left to review, since the judgment depends on the specific task and model, not on a fixed budget this repository could check.
practices/0013: No automated check can tell whether an instruction an author is relying on actually survives compaction in a given project; enforcement is left to review, since that depends on where the instruction lives, not on anything this repository's own tooling can inspect.
practices/0014: No automated check can measure a project's own runtime or token cost with and without a context file; enforcement is left to review, since that requires running the project's own agent, not anything this repository's tooling can inspect.
practices/0015: No automated check can tell whether a claim about instruction-file structure and compliance is backed by a controlled study; enforcement is left to review, since that requires judging the claim's evidence, not the file's shape.
practices/0016: No automated check can measure a project's own patch coverage or precision with and without refined guidance; enforcement is left to review, since that requires running the project's own agent against its own benchmark.
practices/0017: No automated check can tell whether a project's context file actually covers security and performance guidance; enforcement is left to review, since that requires reading what the file says, not just that it exists.
antipatterns/0001: No automated check can reliably detect a repository-overview section by structure alone; enforcement is left to review, since a heuristic strict enough to catch it would also catch legitimate architectural documentation.
antipatterns/0002: No automated check can reliably count how much emphasis is too much in prose; enforcement is left to review, since a heuristic strict enough to catch pervasive emphasis would also flag the sparing, single-line use this repository's own sourced guidance recommends.
antipatterns/0003: No automated check can tell whether an AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md file was LLM-generated and left unedited; enforcement is left to review, since that requires judging the file's content, not a structural signature it leaves behind.
antipatterns/0004: No automated check can tell whether an environment-variable opt-in instruction in a project's own files is stale; enforcement is left to review, since that requires knowing the tool's current default, not anything visible in the file itself.
antipatterns/0005: No automated check can tell whether two tables in different documents carry the same information; enforcement is left to review, since that requires comparing meaning across files, not just detecting that two tables exist.
antipatterns/0006: No automated check can tell whether a metric or count design conflates a genuine zero with a collection failure; enforcement is left to review, since that requires understanding what the metric is meant to measure, not its numeric output.
antipatterns/0007: No automated check can tell whether anything downstream reads a generated record; enforcement is left to review, since that requires knowing the whole pipeline a project runs, not just the record's existence.
antipatterns/0008: No automated check here inspects an external project's instruction file for addendum-section growth; this repository's own no-addendum-sections check only scans this repository's own tracked files, not the files another project's author is writing.
